Maybe not straight up, but something like a 20° incline. Would you hit space? Would gravity slow it down too much to get far enough out?
What would happen if you kept flying an airplane upwards?
The limiting factor is air density. Eventually you'll reach a point where there's not enough air to hold the plane up. And not enough air intake into the engines to keep them going.

It would eventually just stall. Most planes use air-breathing engines. Once you reach a certain altitude where the air is too thin for the engine to suck up enough to continue running, it stalls. Gravity has nothing to do with it really, other than the role it plays AFTER the engine stalls, in which it would bring you back down to Earth. You would never ever hit space in an airplane that uses an air-breathing engine, regardless of your incline.

The escape velocity of the Earth is roughly 25,000 miles per hour. So you could get to a very high altitude, but not too far out of the atmosphere. Gravity would slow you down too much to "get out" if you mean actually being able to leave Earth float around space not captured by Earth's gravity.
Play Kerbal Space Program and find out!

Engines lose their efficiency (and thus the majority of their power) as the air gets thinner. Air is taken in and goes through several compression stages while fuel is injected and ignited. If the engines have insufficient air intake (because air thins out dramatically with higher altitudes), then they can no longer perform fuel combustion in the engine, and they "flame out" or cease to operate. Rockets don't have this problem, because the fuel they use contains so much combustible oxygen or other combustible fuel that they can carry their own combustion source with them all the way into space. Other planes have to get it from the surrounding atmosphere. If the atmosphere disappears, so does combustion.

Another reason planes can't fly into space is because when they reach a certain altitude, the air becomes so thin that the control surfaces on the plane that let the pilot steer it and keep it pointed where it should be cease to be effective, and the plane just starts spinning out of control.
